analysis.investment_thesis: Kirloskar Brothers is a genuinely durable, improving business — but at 25.4x EV/EBITDA and a 2.1% FCF yield (INR 297 Cr FCF on INR 14,010 Cr market cap), the price already reflects near-perfection, leaving no margin of safety. With 9-year revenue CAGR of only 6.1%, the market is paying a premium growth multiple for a sub-growth business, betting the margin expansion story runs further — a bet I'm unwilling to make at this price.
key_strengths: Margin transformation is remarkable: EBITDA margin expanded from 5.3% (2016) to 14.7% (2025), with EBITDA CAGR of 18.7% over 9 years
Fortress balance sheet: Debt/Equity of 0.10, net cash of ~INR 141 Cr (cash INR 323 Cr vs debt INR 182 Cr), financing costs falling at -7.6% CAGR
Consistent cash generation: OCF positive 5/5 years, FCF doubled from INR 168 Cr (FY20) to INR 297 Cr (FY25); ROCE of 27.6% is excellent for industrials
key_risks: Revenue growth is structurally modest at 6.1% 9Y CAGR — the re-rating was driven by margin expansion, which is harder to repeat from 14.7% margins vs. earlier 5%
FCF yield of 2.1% offers no margin of safety; price would need to fall ~65-70% to hit Howard Marks' 6-8% FCF yield threshold
Government infrastructure and water capex dependency makes this cyclical — any slowdown in Jal Jeevan Mission or irrigation spending hits revenue disproportionately
red_flags: At 33.9x P/E with 6% revenue CAGR, consensus is pricing in indefinite margin and earnings momentum — classic late-cycle optimism
EV/EBITDA of 25.4x for specialty industrial machinery implies zero room for error in execution or cycle
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Second-level question: everyone knows Kirloskar Brothers has improved dramatically — EBITDA up 4.7x since 2016, net profit turned from -INR 23 Cr to +INR 419 Cr. But what does the price already reflect? At INR 14,010 Cr market cap against INR 297 Cr of FCF, the implied FCF yield is 2.1% — roughly a 50x FCF multiple. My minimum acceptable FCF yield is 6-8%, implying fair value somewhere in the INR 3,700-5,000 Cr range on current earnings power. The stock trades at nearly 3x that. The business earned this re-rating through genuine operational improvement, but the re-rating is now complete and the price has run ahead of intrinsic value.

The stress scenario is what disciplines me here. If government infrastructure spending cools — a real risk given India's fiscal consolidation pressures — revenue, which grew at only 6.1% even during the good years, could stagnate. At 14.7% EBITDA margins, there is less operating leverage cushion than there was at 5% margins in 2016. An EBITDA compression back toward 10-11% margins on flat revenue would produce EBITDA of ~INR 450-500 Cr, supporting a 15-18x fair EV/EBITDA of roughly INR 7,500-9,000 Cr — implying meaningful downside from today. The 137-year-old franchise, low leverage, and strong promoter holding (65.95%) are genuine qualities, but great businesses at wrong prices remain wrong investments. I wait for price to meet value, not the reverse.
